title: Petty cash book
body_markdown:
Reggie maintains a petty cash book using the imprest system. The imprest amount is $250 and is restored on the first day of each month. 
 All payments of less than $50 are made from petty cash. 
 All cash receipts of less than $50 are paid into petty cash.
 On 1 April 2026, Reggie had $133 in his petty cash box. He provided the following information for April 2026. 
 April 
1.   Restored petty cash imprest from the business bank account 
5   Paid $40 to Greta, a trade payable 
9   Paid $16 for cleaning materials 
15   Received $31 from Awez, a trade receivable 
20   Paid $11 for postage 
27   Paid $42 wages to the cleaner of the business premises 
29   Paid $23 for printer paper 
 REQUIRED 
(a) Prepare Reggie's petty cash book for the month of April 2026. 
 Balance the petty cash book and bring down the balance at May 2026.
 The amount of cash drawn from the bank account to restore the imprest on April has been omitted from the cash book. When Reggie received his bank statement dated 30 April 2026, he 2 identified an unpresented cheque for $390 and an uncredited deposit of $450. The bank balance 2 shown on the bank statement is a positive balance of $982.
 REQUIRED 
(b) Calculate the bank balance which was shown in the cash book at 30 April 2026. 
 Reggie is considering using petty cash for receipts and payments of under $10 only. All other receipts would be required by bank transfer and all other payments would be made by bank transfer. The imprest amount would be reduced to $100. 
 REQUIRED 
(c) Advise Reggie whether or not he should require that all receipts over $10 are made by bank transfer and make all payments over $10 by bank transfer. Justify your answer by providing both advantages and disadvantages of making this change.

title: Principles
body_markdown:
A business purchased a set of rulers that cost $9. The set of rulers was expected to last for several years, but the business did not treat it as a non-current asset.
 Which accounting principle was the business following?
A  business entity
B  going concern 
C  materiality 
D  realisation

title: Priciples
body_markdown:
A business included all wages due, but unpaid, in its income statement for the year. 
 Which accounting principle was being followed? 
A  going concern 
B  matching 
C  materiality 
D  realisation

title: Cost Principle
body_markdown:
Which statement describes the historic cost principle? 
A  All assets and expenses are initially recorded at their original price. 
B  Businesses only record transactions which can be expressed in terms of money. 
C  Costs are recognised when they are incurred, not when the money is paid. 
D  It is assumed that the business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future.

title: Relevance
body_markdown:
Which statement describes 'relevance' as an objective when selecting accounting policies?
A  Accounting information must be accurate. 
B  Accounting information must be free from bias. 
C  Accounting information must influence users' decisions.
D  Accounting information must stay consistent over time.
